title: State Police trooper suspended after allegedly stealing Bobcat excavator
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: State Trooper Joseph Franklin charged with theft of a Bobcat excavator; arraigned and pleaded not guilty in Palmer District Court.
Franklin's police certification was suspended by POST Commission due to possible criminal conduct; he remains suspended with pay.
Dispute arose from tree removal job; police recovered the Bobcat after it was reported stolen by the contractor.

title: All the new movies and TV shows streaming now (August 2026)
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: "Ted Lasso" Season 4 premieres on Apple TV on August 5, with Jason Sudeikis coaching the AFC Richmond women's team.
"Reacher" Season 4 releases on Prime Video on August 14, starring Alan Ritchson in a vigilante justice storyline.
Netflix debuts "The Whisper Man" starring Robert De Niro, Michelle Monaghan, and Adam Scott on August 29.

title: A longtime 7News reporter is signing off
author: John Waller
bullets: Kimberly Bookman is leaving 7News after 12 years, with her last day on air announced for Tuesday.
Bookman, a Needham native, joined 7News in 2014 and has previously worked in New Hampshire, Maryland, South Carolina, and New York.
Bookman plans to remain local and highlighted her training of new reporters and annual clothing drive efforts in her farewell post.

title: Cambridge man dies after being pulled from waters off Martha’s Vineyard
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Kevin Foster, 55, died after being pulled from waters off Martha's Vineyard, per Cape & Islands District Attorney's Office.
Emergency responders and lifeguards rescued multiple distressed swimmers at Long Point Wildlife Refuge in West Tisbury.
State Rep. Marjorie Decker launched a GoFundMe for Foster's family, raising over $74,000 after the incident.

title: Drake Maye runs through scouting report of Patriots’ crowded receiver room
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Drake Maye reviewed each of the seven wide receivers vying for spots in the New England Patriots' offense.
Patriots' wide receiver room includes A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Kayshon Boutte, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams.
Maye highlighted A.J. Brown's playmaking and leadership, indicating a competitive drive within the receiver group.

title: Why one MLB analyst labeled Red Sox trade for Adley Rutschman as a ‘wild overpay on the face of it’
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Red Sox acquired Adley Rutschman from Orioles for Carlos Narváez and prospects, plus potential player or cash considerations.
ESPN analyst Kiley McDaniel called the trade a 'wild overpay,' questioning Boston's aggressive strategy.
Red Sox aimed to boost offense following Curtis Mead's injury, which impacted team performance metrics.

title: David Sedaris on Duolingo, death, and dressing like a priest
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: David Sedaris releases new essay collection 'The Land and Its People,' featuring humorous insights and personal stories.
Sedaris discusses his journey with Duolingo addiction and newfound freedom from leaderboard pressures.
The author reflects on family dynamics, including strained relationships and themes of aging and death in his work.

title: John C. Reilly jumped on stage to sing at a Boston dive bar
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: Actor John C. Reilly performed two songs at Tavern at the End of the World in Boston.
Reilly joined local band Bosstown Heavy for Toots and the Maytals' '54-46 (That's My Number)'.
Reilly visited Kelly's Diner in Somerville for breakfast following his late-night dive bar performance.

title: Mass. woman found after going missing for 27 hours in N.H. woods
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Megan Kelley, 39, of Massachusetts, went missing from Dolly Copp Campground, New Hampshire on Saturday.
A hiking couple found Kelley on an access road near Gorham after 27 hours missing.
Kelley, found immobile but not seriously injured, was taken to Androscoggin Valley Hospital.

title: Plymouth woman dies after tree falls on her porch
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: A 61-year-old Plymouth woman died after a tree fell on her porch during strong winds, according to officials.
Emergency responders arrived at Sullivan Avenue around 1:10 p.m. Monday, finding the woman trapped by the tree.
Authorities are investigating, with preliminary findings suggesting heavy rains and wind caused the tree to fall.
